extra.message: Single static shared-secret gate protects all critical ops endpoints with no additional hardening — If the shared INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN is guessed, brute-forced (no rate limiting), or leaked via any of the sibling endpoints, an attacker gains unauthenticated access to RCE, arbitrary file write, XXE and NoSQL injection primitives [verified: _wrk_gate is a single static shared-secret string compare (no rate limiting, no per-caller identity) guarding all RCE/file-write/XXE/NoSQL endpoints.]

Insecure deserialization via pickle.loads on request body — Remote code execution on the application server via a crafted pickle payload [verified: request.body/GET-controlled bytes reach pickle.loads directly behind only the static header gate; no validation exists.]

Code injection via eval() of user-supplied expression — Arbitrary code execution by breaking out of the restricted eval sandbox [verified: user 'expr' from GET reaches eval() with empty __builtins__, which is a well-known bypassable sandbox.]

Path traversal leading to arbitrary file write — Arbitrary file write anywhere the app process can write, potentially overwriting application code or planting a webshell [verified: 'name' GET param is concatenated into BASE_EXPORT_DIR with no path sanitization before write_bytes.]

NoSQL injection via unrestricted MongoDB filter from request body — Bypass intended query logic, extract arbitrary records, or trigger server-side JS execution via $where [verified: raw JSON body's 'filter' key is passed unchecked to MongoClient find_one, permitting operator injection.]

XXE via lxml parser with entity resolution enabled — Local file disclosure, SSRF, or denial of service via XML external entities [verified: lxml XMLParser explicitly sets load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False on attacker-controlled request.body.]

Privilege escalation via client-controlled cookie/header value — Any caller who passes the internal-token gate can self-elevate to a privileged data lane by setting a trivial cookie/header [verified: Elevation to 'elevated' lane is gated solely on a client-supplied cookie/header equal to a static string, no identity/session check.]

Privilege escalation via trivially forgeable badge cookie/header — Attacker self-escalates to an elevated data-access lane exposing payroll and casework information by supplying a guessable static value [verified: duplicate of idx 9: static-string cookie/header self-elevation with no server-side identity check.]

Insecure-by-default settings: hardcoded SECRET_KEY fallback and DEBUG defaults to True — Known SECRET_KEY allows session/cookie forgery and signed-token tampering; DEBUG=True in production leaks source code, settings, and stack traces via Django error pages [verified: Both SECRET_KEY hardcoded fallback and DEBUG defaulting to True are present in code at settings.py:11-12 with no override enforced elsewhere; deployments that omit env vars run insecure by default.]

Hardcoded fallback Django SECRET_KEY — An attacker who knows the fallback key can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens, leading to full authentication bypass and account takeover [verified: Hardcoded fallback SECRET_KEY string is present verbatim at line 11 with no additional check preventing its use in production.]

DEBUG defaults to True when env var unset — Unauthenticated attackers triggering an unhandled exception see full stack traces, local variables, request data, and installed app/settings info, aiding further attacks and leaking secrets/PII from tracebacks [verified: DEBUG default is literally the string "True" at line 12 with no other gating logic forcing it False in deployment, confirmed genuinely present.]

Reflected XSS via unescaped GET parameter in ops caption endpoint — Attacker-controlled JavaScript executes in the context of whoever/whatever renders this ops HTML response (browser-based internal tooling), enabling session/token theft or further pivoting against internal operators [verified: duplicate of idx 5: unescaped GET param concatenated into HTML response.]

Sensitive data exposure: PII/secret token returned in ops response — Disclosure of client tax identifier (PII) and a live partner sync credential to any holder of the internal ops token [verified: endpoint returns a live-looking partner token and SSN-like tax_ref to any caller passing only the shared ops gate.]

Sensitive Authorization header and body logged in cleartext — Credential/token leakage to anyone with log access, enabling session/account takeover [verified: logger.warning logs full request body and raw Authorization header verbatim.]

CORS misconfiguration: reflected origin with credentials allowed — Any malicious website can read authenticated responses from this endpoint on behalf of a victim browser [verified: Origin header is reflected verbatim into Access-Control-Allow-Origin alongside Allow-Credentials: true.]

Disabled TLS certificate verification on outbound request — Man-in-the-middle attackers can intercept or tamper with the outbound connection to the partner endpoint [verified: ssl._create_unverified_context() is used for an outbound urlopen call, disabling certificate verification.]

Secure cookie flags and TLS redirect gated behind DEBUG, which defaults to insecure — Session and CSRF cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP and intercepted by a network attacker [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE/SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT are only set inside `if not DEBUG:` at line 109, and DEBUG defaults to True, so these protections are absent by default.]

CSV Formula Injection in matter/deadline/document export — When a privileged user (firm admin/attorney/paralegal) opens the exported CSV in Excel/Sheets, malicious formulas can trigger data exfiltration, legacy DDE command execution, or phishing via HYPERLINK. [verified: Same root cause confirmed: _csv_response performs no sanitization and export views pass through attacker-editable title/tag fields, enabling formula payloads like =HYPERLINK(...).]

CSV/Excel formula injection in report exports — Arbitrary formula/DDE execution in the spreadsheet application of any staff user who opens matter/document/deadline CSV exports, potentially leading to local code execution, credential theft, or SSRF from the victim's machine (classic CSV injection) [verified: Confirmed same missing-sanitization sink; import path adds an additional injection vector but the core CSV export vulnerability is independently valid regardless of import.]

Cookie set without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite flags — Cookie can be exposed over plaintext HTTP or accessed by client-side script, aiding session/cookie theft [verified: set_cookie called with no secure/httponly/samesite flags.]

Weak PRNG used for security-sensitive code generation — Predictable codes/tokens if the internal PRNG state is inferred, undermining any security property relying on unpredictability [verified: random.choice (Mersenne Twister) is used to generate a 'code' intended as a secret/nonce.]

Non-constant-time verifier comparison and weak PRNG for generated codes — Predictable/guessable tokens (random.choice is not cryptographically secure) could allow forging one-time codes; timing side channel on verifier check aids brute force [verified: verifier compared with != (non-constant-time) and nonce generated with non-CSPRNG random module.]
